feed.title: Windhawk Mod Updates
feed.subtitle: Updates in the official collection of Windhawk mods

entry.title: On-Screen Indicator Position 1.5.0
entry.content:
• Each indicator can now use its own horizontal and vertical offset, including zero, or keep the main offset.
  • Each indicator can be left at the Windows default position on its own; the offsets still apply to it.
  • New display profiles change placement by monitor name, number of monitors in use, and indicator.
  • New Seconds on screen setting changes how long the indicator stays up, from 1 to 60 seconds. When it is off, the mod leaves Explorer's timers alone.
  • Offsets are scaled using the actual scale of the monitor the indicator is on.

entry.title: Disable Task Manager Navigation Border 0.1
entry.content:
Disable Task Manager Navigation Border

Disables the ugly focus borders in Windows 11 Task Manager.

It works by replacing the following functions with empty implementations:

  • AtmView::SetBorderUponNavigationForColumnHeader
  • AtmView::SetBorderUponNavigationForListRow
  • AtmView::SetBorderUponNavigationForListRowWithColumnTraversal
  • SetBorderUponNavigatingIntoElement

Functions are located using symbols for the running Taskmgr.exe version, not fixed addresses. First use may require internet access to download symbols. Initialization fails if any required symbol is unavailable.

This MOD targets x64 Task Manager versions providing these methods. No system files or signatures are modified.

禁用 Windows 11 任务管理器上丑陋的焦点边框。

实现原理是将以下方法替换为空实现：

  • AtmView::SetBorderUponNavigationForColumnHeader
  • AtmView::SetBorderUponNavigationForListRow
  • AtmView::SetBorderUponNavigationForListRowWithColumnTraversal
  • SetBorderUponNavigatingIntoElement

这些函数是通过当前运行的 Taskmgr.exe 版本的符号信息进行定位，而非固定内存地址。首次使用可能需要联网下载符号文件。若缺少任何所需符号，初始化将失败。

此 MOD 适用于包含上述方法的 x64 版本任务管理器。不会修改任何系统文件或签名。

entry.title: Flashlight Desktop Icons 1.0.0
entry.content:
Flashlight Desktop Icons

Makes desktop icons semi-transparent (or completely invisible) when idle. When the mouse cursor moves over the desktop, only the icons within the configured pixel radius smoothly reveal themselves, and they fade back to their idle opacity once the mouse stops moving.

  • No overlay windows: each icon's alpha is applied at draw time with GDI custom draw, so nothing blocks clicks and no wallpaper layers are duplicated. Compatible with Wallpaper Engine and other live wallpapers.
  • No background threads and no polling: repainting is driven by mouse events and a fade timer running on the desktop's own thread, so the mod does no work at all while the mouse is away from the desktop.
  • Labels fade together with their icons. Enable the "Hide Icon Labels" setting to remove the text under desktop icons entirely.
  • Dragging a file over the desktop reveals the icons around the drag cursor, so you can see what you are dropping onto.
  • Double-clicking empty desktop space hides all icons; double-clicking again returns to flashlight mode (rather than making all icons fully visible).

How this differs from similar mods

  • Transparent Desktop Icons with Spotlight reveals icons around the cursor using a DirectComposition overlay mask. This mod instead computes each icon's alpha from its distance to the cursor and applies it per icon at draw time (GDI custom draw), with no overlay or wallpaper layers.
  • Desktop Icons Transparency applies one fixed opacity to all desktop icons. This mod's opacity is per-icon and follows the cursor.
  • Desktop Icon Section Auto-Hide & Fluent Hover Reveal and ZenDesktop hide and reveal icons in bulk (per section or on toggle). This mod's default experience is a continuous visibility gradient around the cursor.

Known limitations

  • Faded labels are drawn in the mod's own style (white text with a glow) rather than Explorer's shadow style, so a label changes slightly when its icon reaches full opacity and Explorer takes over drawing it.

Credits

  • desktop-icons-transparency by zed712969-crypto: desktop window discovery and subclassing patterns.
  • Smooth Desktop Icons Auto-Hide by HeyOkay: the drag-and-drop reveal approach (hooking the desktop's IDropTarget vtable methods).

entry.title: Custom Cached Context Menu 1.1.1
entry.content:
Added

  • A "Background pre-build" setting (on by default). Turning it off skips the startup warm-up, which is an extra moment where every registered context-menu handler is loaded; handlers then load only for menus that open, as with the stock menu. This avoids startup crashes from faulty third-party extensions, while a handler that would crash the stock menu still does when its menu is built. The first open of each context builds on demand; later opens stay instant. The mod's own New submenu and Send to entries are unaffected: their lists are built by the invalidation thread, which always runs.

Fixed

  • Extension items on a folder background now invoke their verb on the current folder directly when the folder registration runs the same command, instead of going through the deferred menu population.
  • Labels that embed the selected file's name (for example NanaZip's "Extract to """) are cached as templates and re-rendered with the current name, so they no longer show a previous file's name and their invocation matches again. Only the start of a quoted label segment is templated, and folders keep their full name. Existing caches rebuild once after the update.
  • The per-thread bitmap and owner-subclass buffers are released on unload instead of staying on Explorer's long-lived UI threads.

Changed

  • Debug logging now reports when a live-menu match was found but its invocation failed.

entry.title: Alt.Binz Dark Mode 1.0.0
entry.content:
Alt.Binz Dark Mode

Alt.Binz draws its whole user interface from a light blue skin. This mod re-colors everything that is drawn with GDI: brushes, pens, text colors, system colors and the opaque skin bitmaps. Common dialogs and shell menus keep Windows' own dark mode.

Compatibility

Tested with Alt.Binz 0.48.4 (32-bit) at 100% display scaling on Windows 11. Some elements (the column header bars, the progress bar fills and the status bar button) are recognized by their size and color, so another version may look different.

Surface color

The blue skin surface (toolbar, tabs, status bar, dialogs, Setup) can get another color: enter a hex code (for example 2F5A96). Very bright colors are darkened so that the light text stays readable.

Surface gradient

Instead of one color the surface can run between two colors. Enter both as hex codes, the angle in degrees (0 = left to right, 90 = top to bottom) and the balance: 50 is the middle, a higher value gives the end color more room, a lower value the start color. The gradient wins over the single surface color.

Progress bars

The fill of the progress bars can get one color or, with a second color, a gradient, either from top to bottom or from left to right. Leave both empty for the default blue.

Appearance

These values are applied when Alt.Binz is restarted:

  • Background lightness: how dark the lists and dark areas are (percent).
  • Text lightness: how bright text and lines are (percent). Ignored when a text color is set.
  • Text color: an optional color for text and lines.
  • List background color: an optional color for the large list areas.
  • Saturation: how colorful the blue skin is (percent).

The column header color (the header bars of the lists) and everything else is applied live. If you disable the mod, restart Alt.Binz to get the original look back completely.

entry.title: Tray hover expand 1.7.1
entry.content: • Do not suppress hover when the taskbar itself is visible under the cursor, so an auto-hiding taskbar works as soon as it is revealed, and a maximized window is no longer mistaken for a fullscreen app

entry.title: PaintShop Pro Dark Image Windows 1.0.0
entry.content:
PaintShop Pro Dark Image Windows

Corel PaintShop Pro has a dark theme, but the image windows inside the workspace keep a light blue-gray frame that looks like Windows XP or 7. They are classic MDI child windows, and Windows draws their frames itself, with no dark variant.

This mod paints those frames in dark colors instead:

  • title bar, border, icon and title text
  • minimize, maximize and close buttons with hover and pressed states
  • minimized image windows

Maximized image windows are left to Windows. Everything is drawn by the mod, so no theme files or system settings are touched, and the mod only affects PaintShop Pro.

Optional flash fix

When you switch between images, PaintShop Pro rebuilds the drop-down lists in the tool options bar. For a few frames their selection fields flash white, because the Windows combo box falls back to its default brush. The flash fix paints that field in dark gray instead.

Settings

All colors are entered as hex codes, for example 282828 or #282828. A value that cannot be read falls back to its default. Changes apply right away.

Notes

  • Tested with PaintShop Pro 2022 on Windows 11. Other versions may work, but have not been tested.
  • If something looks wrong, disable the mod: the original frames come back immediately.

entry.title: Modern Run Dialog UI For Windows 10 & 11 3.0.6
entry.content:
Fixed an issue on Windows 11 build 26300.9807+ where the classic Run dialog appeared when shell32.pdb symbols were unavailable on Microsoft's symbol server (HTTP 404), by adding an automatic symbol-less hooking fallback (DialogBoxParamW, DialogBoxIndirectParamW, CreateDialogParamW, CreateDialogIndirectParamW, and ShowWindow) (#6544).

Added experimental PowerToys Run-style app and command suggestions while typing (enableAppSuggestions), indexing Start Menu shortcuts, Registry App Paths, built-in system tools, and recent history with lazy icon loading and keyboard/mouse navigation (Up/Down, Tab to autocomplete, Enter or click to launch).

Restored the distinct high-contrast colors and Direct2D vector icons for the 3 bottom action buttons (Browse with folder icon, Run in Fluent Blue with return arrow icon, and Exit in dark crimson with close icon) across all surface themes including Liquid Glass, with dynamic button width adaptation for localized labels.

Added 10 new display languages (totaling 21 languages): Thai (th), Indonesian (id), Malay (ms), Portuguese (pt), Ukrainian (uk), Polish (pl), Dutch (nl), Turkish (tr), Hindi (hi), and Arabic (ar).

entry.title: App Volume Booster 1.0
entry.content:
App Volume Booster

Changes the loudness of the audio an app sends to Windows, so it can go past the 100% limit of the volume mixer.

This mod doesn't target any process by default.

Which apps: open this mod's Advanced tab -> Custom process inclusion list and list the exe names you want affected (one per line). Only those processes get the mod. Restart an app after adding it to the list.

Note for games: Games are excluded by default in Windhawk. To work with games, they need to be specifically added to the inclusion list from Windhawk's Advanced settings: Settings > Advanced settings > More advanced settings > Process Inclusion List.

How loud: every included app uses the default settings. To give one app its own settings, click + under Per-app overrides, type its exe name and choose its volume and mode. An override only applies to apps that are also in the inclusion list. Overrides with an empty process name are ignored.

Modes

  • Gain (default): multiplies the audio by the volume %. 100 = unchanged, 200 = twice as loud. Anything pushed past full scale is clipped.
  • Compressor: turns down the loud parts, then applies the volume % as makeup gain, so quiet material gets louder with less distortion on loud peaks. Tune it with threshold, ratio, attack and release (these settings are shared by all apps).

Changes apply live. Lower your system volume before starting, boosted audio can be very loud. Exclusive-mode streams, spatial audio streams (e.g. Windows Sonic / Dolby Atmos, which bypass IAudioRenderClient), and apps that bypass WASAPI entirely may not be affected.

Troubleshooting: start the app after enabling the mod (streams created earlier are not seen), then check Windhawk's log for this mod. It reports each stream's format and whether audio is being processed.

entry.title: GPU-accelerated explorer.exe list and grid views 0.9.240
entry.content:
GPU-accelerated explorer.exe list and grid views

A Windhawk mod for Windows 11 Explorer with GPU rendering for smooth animations and modern look.

  • Replicates explorer views using hardware accelerated graphics: Details list and icons grid, including thumbnails, sorting and grouping.
  • Animated interactions: grouping, sorting, selecting/cutting/copying files, and many more.
  • Smooth scrolling, touchpad gestures and inertia scrolling.
  • RTL language support.
  • Optional button to switch back to native Explorer view; Ctrl+Alt+F9 also works when the button is hidden.
  • Prioritizes responsiveness and animations over efficiency.
  • Less likely to break in future Windows updates since it does not modify the default views of explorer but recreates them

Features

  • Adjustable Item Height — Smooth zooming with Ctrl+ mouse wheel or pinch gestures.
  • Custom Fonts — Personalize the appearance with your preferred fonts.
  • Text Antialiasing — Use Windows monitor tuning, smooth grayscale, or no antialiasing while preserving transparent backgrounds.
  • Animated Selection & Hover States — Smooth visual transitions, including a dedicated selection style for file names only.
  • Dynamic Zebra Striping — Animated alternating row colors for improved readability.
  • Smooth Scrolling — Fluid scrolling for a more responsive browsing experience.
  • Seamless View Switching — Overlays the default Explorer views, letting you switch between the modded and native views directly from the Explorer window.
  • Faster Loading — Improves load times through caching and by skipping file pre-sorting.
  • Adaptive Image Quality — Matches icon and thumbnail resolution to visible size and available memory.

Report bugs

Report bugs in the mod's main repository Here. Enable Enable logging when reproducing a bug and include Windhawk's log in the report. Logs include file names and paths; disable the option afterward.

entry.title: Window Rules 1.0
entry.content:
Window Rules

Tell Windows what to do with an app's windows, once, and stop fixing them by hand. Each rule matches a window (by executable, window class and title) and asks for one or more of:

  • a position and size, in pixels
  • a monitor to open on
  • an opacity level
  • always on top

Rules are tried in order. The first enabled rule that matches a window is the only one applied to it -- later rules are not consulted for that window, and actions are never merged across rules. That is the same model KWin rules and WindowManager use, and it is the one that stays predictable when two of your rules would both apply.

What it does

Open the app and the rule happens: the window is moved, sized and made translucent where the rule says so. Move the window yourself and the mod lets go -- your position wins for the rest of the session, and the rule is not re-applied to that window until the app is started again. Saving the settings re-applies every rule to the windows that are open at that moment, so editing a rule shows you its effect immediately instead of at the next restart.

Nothing else is touched: no focus, no hiding, and no continuous watch over windows that are already in place.

Always on top

A rule can keep an app's windows above other windows. The window goes up when it opens and stays up: activating another window does not take the top away, because Windows keeps a window's topmost bit until something actually removes it.

What it deliberately does not do is fight for the top:

  • Another always-on-top window can sit above yours. The taskbar and other pinned apps are the user's own choices, and the mod does not climb back over them.
  • A fullscreen app on the same monitor makes it step aside. A window pinned by this mod is lowered while a fullscreen game or video covers its monitor, and raised again when that app is gone. A maximized window is not fullscreen and never triggers this.
  • If the app clears the bit itself, the mod leaves it cleared, and the journal says app-cleared, rather than pinning it again on the next activation.
  • Dragging the window stops the mod touching it, the z-order included, for the rest of the session.
  • Turning the rule off takes the window back down. The mod only ever lowers a bit it set itself, so an app that pins its own windows is never affected.
  • The same goes for opacity. The mod records the windows it made translucent, so changing the level takes effect on windows that are already open, and clearing the level, deleting the rule or turning the mod off puts them back to fully opaque. Only windows the mod faded itself are touched: an app that draws its own transparency is never made opaque by this.

One consequence worth knowing before you pin something: a topmost window stays above whatever you switch to with Alt+Tab, so if the pinned window covers most of the screen, switching away looks like nothing happened -- the window you wanted is behind it. That is how the topmost bit works, not something this mod adds. Pin small windows, or leave the rule on "No change" while you are switching around.

Where windows go, and in what units

Positions and sizes are in physical pixels, not points. A rule that says 800x600 gets a window 800 physical pixels wide whatever the display scale is, so on a 150% display it will look smaller than the same rule on a 100% one. That is not adjustable in this version, and it is the same truth the whole mod works in: the mod reads and writes physical pixels, and reports them in the journal so that what it did can be checked by hand.

A position is measured from the top-left of the target monitor, not from the desktop. position: 100,200 means 100 pixels in and 200 down from the corner of the monitor the rule names -- or of the monitor the window is already on, when the rule names none. So a rule survives docking, undocking and adding a monitor above the primary, which the same numbers in desktop coordinates would not. X and Y may be negative to place a window partly off the edge.

How matching works

A rule has three optional match fields. Every field you fill in must match; a field you leave blank matches anything. The fields are:

  • Executable -- a file name (notepad or notepad.exe) or a full path.
  • Window class -- the window's class name, for example Notepad or Chrome_WidgetWin_1.
  • Window title -- searched inside the title, so a fragment is enough.

All matching is case-insensitive. * and ? are wildcards, so chrome* matches chrome.exe and Untitled* matches any title starting that way. To use a full regular expression, wrap it in slashes: /^Document - \w+\.txt$/. Nothing else is treated as a pattern, so a path like C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steam.exe or a title like Inbox | Outlook matches literally.

What it does not do, and where the limits are

  • Hide a window from the taskbar or Alt+Tab. Toggling the extended window style is one-shot and applications reset it themselves; a version that cannot re-assert would be a broken promise, so it is not here yet.
  • Move windows between virtual desktops: that needs an undocumented Windows interface, and this mod does not use one.
  • Override an app that insists. A rule is applied when the window appears and re-applied once if the app immediately moves it somewhere else. An app that moves its window again after that wins -- the mod stops rather than fighting it.
  • A rule waits for a minimized window to be restored. A minimized window has no meaningful rectangle to move, so nothing is applied while it is minimized; the rule is applied the moment you restore it, including for an app that starts in the tray.
  • A maximized window stays maximized. The mod does not restore it to normal first, and what Windows does with a maximized window's restore rectangle is Windows' business rather than the mod's, so a rule that sets a position may not show until you restore the window yourself.
  • Opacity on a window that is already translucent by itself. Those windows draw their own transparency; a flat opacity level would replace it with something that renders wrong, so the mod reports already-layered in the journal and leaves them alone.
  • Change a window's size when the app is in charge of it. Some apps re-create their window when resized; they are left as they are after the single retry.
  • The invisible border. Since Windows 10 a window's rectangle includes about seven pixels of invisible resize border on the left, right and bottom, so position: 0,0 leaves a small visible gap at the left, and an 800x600 window looks about 14 pixels narrower and 7 shorter. The mod does exactly what the numbers say in the coordinates Windows reports, and the journal prints them.
  • File Explorer windows are not matched. explorer.exe is on the built-in exclude list, because the same process owns the taskbar, the desktop and the shell's own windows. Explorer windows cannot be targeted by a rule in this version.
  • A window on another virtual desktop is left alone until you save the settings while it is in front of you. Those windows are cloaked, and the mod ignores cloaked windows on purpose. So if you delete a rule while one of its windows sits on another desktop, that window keeps its opacity and its always on top until the next settings save with it visible, or until you turn the mod off. Nothing is left behind after that.
  • Always on top and fullscreen is detected geometrically. A window counts as fullscreen when it covers a monitor and is not maximized. A window that nearly covers a monitor is not detected, so a pinned window can stay above it.
  • Stepping aside for a fullscreen app is tested, not observed, across monitors. It was built and tried on a single-monitor machine, so "a game on the other monitor leaves this window pinned" has not been watched happening.

Not the same as other mods

  • Always On Top Windows pins and unpins the active window with a hotkey, by hand. This mod keeps an app's windows on top automatically, every time they open.
  • Prevent Focus Stealing and Snap Commander already cover their own actions (focus, and snapping to screen regions) and this mod deliberately does not re-implement them.
  • Where I Left It remembers where you left a window and puts it back. This mod puts a window where you say, every time. Do not list the same app in both mods' settings at once: both would place the window, in an order neither can control. The same goes for Snap Commander's auto-snap rules.

Diagnostics

Write a diagnostics journal appends to window-rules-journal.txt in a folder of your own: <Windhawk mod storage>\<your SID>, created with an access control list that gives full access to you, to SYSTEM and to administrators, and to nobody else. Journal lines carry executable names and window titles, and the shared mod storage folder is readable by every account on the machine, so the file is kept where only you can read it. If that folder cannot be created the journal is simply not written; the mod itself is unaffected.

Neither the file nor the folder exists until you turn the journal on. It is capped at 1 MB (past that it starts again from empty, with a line saying so), and it is off by default; turn it on when a rule does something you did not expect, or when reporting a bug, and the file will say what the mod decided and why. Every line is prefixed with what it is doing:

  • RULES-LOADED and RULE-LOADED -- the rules as the mod understood them, with any problem it found in a rule, so a typo is visible instead of silent.
  • RULE-HIT -- which rule matched which window, and which field decided it.
  • RULE-NONE -- a window that no rule matched (a few per app, not every one).
  • RULE-FILTER-SKIP -- a window that was never matched at all, and why.
  • APPLY -- what was done to a matched window, with the rectangle it was at and the rectangle the rule asked for, and why nothing happened when nothing did (already-there, overridden, minimized, refused).
  • SETTLE -- whether the window stayed where the rule put it, was put back once, or was left alone because the app kept moving it.
  • OVERRIDE -- you moved a window yourself; the mod has let go of it.
  • OPACITY -- what happened to the level, and why: applied, already-there, already-layered (the app draws its own transparency, left alone), failed (the window refused the change), app-cleared (the app removed the style itself), withdrawn (the rule stopped asking, or the mod was turned off).
  • MONITOR-SKIP -- a rule names a monitor that is not there.
  • TOPMOST -- what happened to the z-order, and why: applied, already-there, overridden, minimized, refused, yielded (a fullscreen app took the monitor), reclaimed (it gave the monitor back), app-cleared (the app removed the bit itself), withdrawn (the rule stopped asking), or not-claimed (the window is on top, but this mod did not put it there).
  • REAPPLY-PASS -- the sweep after a settings save, and how many windows it moved.

Settings

Rules are read from the top down, and an entry with every field blank ends the list -- the settings template ships one blank entry, so a fresh install has no rules at all until you fill it in. Leave the blank entry last.

A rule with no match fields is not loaded, because it would apply to every window on the desktop; the journal says RULE-PROBLEM and names the rule. To mean every window on purpose, put a * in one of the match fields.

entry.title: Language Applet Restorer 1.0.0
entry.content:
Language Applet Restorer

Restores the classic Control Panel Language applet from windows 10 1709 and optionally the classic Region applet (intl.cpl) of Windows 10 1709 on later versions of Windows.

Preview:

What is downloaded, from where, and when

The mod does not contain any Microsoft binaries. The first time it runs inside explorer.exe, it downloads five files of Windows 10 1709 (build 16299), about 3.7 MB in total, from Microsoft's public symbol server (https://msdl.microsoft.com/download/symbols/):

intl.cpl, UserLanguagesCpl.dll, WinLangdb.dll, Bcp47Langs.dll and dui70.dll.

The size and SHA-256 of every file are checked against values pinned in the mod, and a file that doesn't match is discarded. The originals are kept in the mod's storage folder (dl); patched copies and small compatibility shims are generated from them into bin. Nothing is downloaded again as long as dl is present.

Offline: if the files are not on disk and there is no internet connection, the applet is simply not added and the reason is written to the mod's log. Connect to the internet and restart explorer.exe once. After a successful first run the mod works offline, provided Keep downloaded files is on.

Settings

  • Page language: language of the restored Language page and its Control Panel tooltip. Automatic follows the Windows UI language. Available: English, Italian, Persian, Spanish, French, Portuguese.
  • Force translations: use the embedded translations for the six languages above, instead of relying only on the generated .mui files.
  • Keep downloaded files when the mod is disabled: keep dl and bin in the storage folder so the mod works offline and doesn't download again. If off, the files are deleted when the mod is unloaded.
  • Redirect Control Panel's intl.cpl to the restored one: when enabled, opening Region (intl.cpl) from Control Panel, the Run dialog or control.exe loads the restored 1709 intl.cpl instead of the system one. This is done in explorer.exe, rundll32.exe and control.exe; the mod does nothing in other processes. It only affects windows opened after the setting is changed. The restored file is checked against the expected contents right before it is loaded; if that fails, or the files are not downloaded yet, the system intl.cpl is used.

Notes

  • Only x64 is supported (no ARM64).
  • The 2017 components run inside explorer.exe. A crash in them restarts Explorer.
  • The mod writes nothing to the user's registry. The applet's registry entries are provided virtually by registry hooks inside explorer.exe (control.exe only gets the part needed to find the applet by name), and the applet's COM classes are created from inside explorer.exe. Every virtual key is handed out as a real, read-only handle to an empty private registry hive (vreg-<pid>.hiv in the mod's storage folder, loaded with RegLoadAppKeyW), so that registry APIs that are not hooked cannot crash on it. The hive is not part of the user's registry, holds no data, and is deleted when the mod is unloaded (leftovers after a crash are removed at the next start). If the hive cannot be loaded, the applet is simply not shown.
  • Compatibility: intl.cpl redirection overlaps with the win7-intl-control-panel-restorer mod. Don't enable the redirect in both mods at the same time: whichever hook runs first decides which intl.cpl is opened.
  • While the mod is enabled, one string in shell32.dll's memory (the applet's entry in Windows' built-in hide list) is blanked so that Control Panel lists the applet. It is restored when the mod is disabled; nothing on disk is changed.
  • Links in the applet that open the Settings app are not changed by this mod. The settings-to-control-panel mod can redirect them.

Special Thanks to:

babamohammed2022 for adding various languages.

entry.title: Simple Cursor Trail 1.6
entry.content:
• Added the "Always on top" setting, enabled by default. The trail now draws above the taskbar, Start menu and other shell surfaces. Explorer hosts a layered, click-through window in the UIAccess Z-order band (falling back to the system-tools band), and the trail is drawn into it; if that is not possible, the trail falls back to its own overlay window.
  • Turning the setting off unloads the explorer.exe side and keeps the trail in the normal desktop band.

entry.title: Hide Taskbar Tooltips 1.3.1
entry.content:
• Add hideStartButtonTooltip setting to hide or show the Windows Start button tooltip independently of taskbar applications.
  • Accurately identify the Start button by querying AutomationProperties.AutomationId == L"StartButton" on the ExperienceToggleButton instance, preventing misclassification of the Task View button.
  • Add tooltipHoverDelayMs setting to configure an extra stationary hover delay (in milliseconds) before showing visible tooltips, while keeping hidden tooltip areas permanently suppressed.
  • Fall back to native display behavior if delayed tooltip scheduling fails or when tooltips open on external Explorer threads to prevent them from being swallowed.
  • Disarm delayed tooltip Win32 timers synchronously on the Shell_TrayWnd UI thread using SendMessageW in Wh_ModBeforeUninit to guarantee all timers are killed before the DLL is unloaded (FreeLibrary).
  • Replace heavy C++/WinRT XAML headers with lightweight ABI COM interfaces, cache IVisualTreeHelperStatics once per visual tree walk, and adopt WRL HString / HStringReference to reduce overhead.
  • Clean up unused -lole32 and -loleaut32 compiler options and remove obsolete #undef GetCurrentTime.

entry.title: Taskbar Thumbnail Stats 1.5
entry.content:
• option to measure RAM as private bytes (like System Informer)
  • CPU is now shown before RAM (configurable) and labels use a colon ("CPU: 3.4% · RAM: 412 MB")
  • "N/A" instead of "…" while the CPU usage is being measured

entry.title: Spotlight Launcher 0.7.1
entry.content:
• A chip for every drive. File mode now shows a chip (with a disk icon) for each of your drives on a second row, kept apart from the location chips so the two groups do not read as one list. A chip is added for every fixed and removable drive that is ready; empty card readers, optical drives with no disc and network drives are skipped, so nothing ever raises a "there is no disk" dialog. The row appears only when you have two or more drives (with a single drive there is nothing to switch to). The chips are detected automatically, no setup.
  • A "This PC" drives view. Going up from a drive root — ← or Backspace on an empty box, or Alt + ↑ — now opens a list of all your drives instead of doing nothing, so you can move between drives with the arrows alone. Enter or → opens the highlighted drive; each row shows its label and free space.
  • Location chips follow moved folders. The Home, Downloads, Documents, Pictures, Music and Videos chips now resolve to each folder's real location, so they still work when a folder has been moved to another drive or redirected (for example a OneDrive-backed Documents).
  • Switch drives with Ctrl + Tab. Ctrl + Tab cycles forward through the drive chips and Ctrl + Shift + Tab backward (the six location chips are left out, since they are a separate idea). Ctrl + 1…9 now jumps to any chip — locations first, then drives — and typing a path such as D:\ in the path bar still works.
  • Start drive setting. A new Start drive option (a single drive letter) chooses which drive the file browser opens on the first time you use it in a session. Empty — or a drive that is not available, such as an unplugged USB stick — opens on Home, as before.
  • The F1 cheat sheet and the README shortcut tables list the new keys.
  • The F1 help sheet no longer resets the bar. It now overlays the current view and closing it returns exactly where you were — the same folder and selection in the file browser, or the calculation you were working on — instead of starting over as if the launcher had just opened.

entry.title: Lock Screen Clock Styler 0.5.0
entry.content:
• Added comprehensive localization for 12 new locales (Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, German, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, French, Italian, Polish, Russian, Ukrainian) alongside English and Turkish (14 languages total).
  • Increased default digit font size from 92 to 140 for improved readability and prominence on modern displays.
  • Enabled live seconds toggle by default across all supported themes.
  • Streamlined feature overview and reordered screenshots showcase to feature Retro Pixel.
  • Clarified glass opacity setting description specifically for Modern Flip cards.
  • Cleaned up unused compiler flags (-lcomctl32).
  • Added Community Contributing & Feedback guidelines.

entry.title: Mac Island & Dock 2.1.0
entry.content:
Folders

  • Sorting by date now finds the newest files in folders with more than 200 items; wider columns.
  • Sorted as in Explorer (name, date modified, type or size, either way, with the date, type or size shown), only one kind of file shown or folders mixed with the files, and each pin with its own icon and color (with an "Apply" button to close the choice); pinned folders show a folder icon again.
  • A file's row has two buttons: copy the file (pasted in a folder, it goes there) and copy its path (#6161).
  • Windows' places open with a click; their pin, at the row's end, pins them (a click used to pin them, #6161).
  • Favorite files: a star on a file's row keeps it with the pinned folders, where a click opens it and its buttons copy the file or its path; one deleted or moved leaves the list, one on a drive taken out comes back with the drive (up to 40).
  • The pins, their icons and colors and the folders' order are each Windows account's own (another account on the same PC no longer shares them).

Calendar

  • Clicking an upcoming event or holiday shows its day in the calendar (#6156).

Notifications

  • With islands on several monitors, the Monitors section chooses which islands show the notifications (the main one by default). The main island keeps the sounds, Windows' banners, Win+N, and calls, alarms and reminders; opening, deleting or minimizing a notification on one island closes it on the others (#6159).
  • The apps with notifications can fold into an arrow, like the tray: they come out a moment when a notification comes, and under the mouse (an option, #6129, #6204, #6208).
  • Chat apps that only blink their tray icon instead of sending notifications to Windows (the Chinese WeChat, WeCom, DingTalk) show on the pill with their dot when it starts blinking (#6074, #6215).

The pill

  • The time can be turned off (on by default, per profile): the date alone shows then, with its own options as before, or nothing when they're off too.
  • A "Show desktop" button for the control center and the pill (off by default).
  • The language bubble only shows when the app in front changes its own mode (Shift, the indicator), not when another app comes in front, and it's no longer cut with a low pill (#6422).
  • An item drawn in two parts (the battery or the volume and its percentage) has one hover highlight (#6460).
  • Win+J (an option, off by default, #6519) minimizes the islands to their line and brings them back; its keys can be changed by recording them in the settings (a click, then the new keys; Win+J back with one click), with a warning when Windows or another app uses them too.
  • With notches, the keyboard language bubble shows once, from the middle notch (#6199).
  • What's playing's note, its cover and title, and its buttons are three items of their own in the pill's order (each placed and turned on or off on its own; current layouts keep them together).
  • A control center button that's on (like night light) shows its icon in the accent color with a dot under it, instead of a white disc behind it.
  • A notification's title too long scrolls under the mouse (#6200).

Media

  • A mixer in the media panel: every app with audio sessions on the default output, one entry per program with its icon, name, volume and mute by clicking the icon; the playing app keeps its own volume and mute in the player, with the device's volume and a button for Windows' mixer below it (Win+Ctrl+V on Windows 11 23H2+, sndvol on older versions or if input fails). The mixer opens collapsed and expands with an animated arrow. The session list and icon conversion are shared with the control center.
  • Source chips show the apps' icons, dimmed when paused, and Automatic has its own glyph. They wrap into more rows when needed.
  • A larger cover, the whole modal tinted from the cover's average color with a smooth color transition, a small app icon beside its name, and two pill switches with rounded highlights in a compact footer; the panel scrolls for long lists and stays within its monitor, with press and spring animations, crossfading/sliding media source transitions and animated mute icons/volume bars.
  • Volume sliders follow the pointer while dragging; audio writes are coalesced off the drawing thread, the mixer reveal keeps its existing row geometry, and footer labels have padding on both sides. Accent colors, media text and icons are cached outside drawing; idle monitor/notch profiles are skipped by the animation loop.
  • Lyrics default to Follows the line (each line's own width, up to 360 DIPs); Short, Medium and Long hold the widest line until a pause or gap.

Credits

  • The README's credits (English and Portuguese) link m417z's mod and ask for credit, with a link, from anyone reusing this mod's code or inspired by it (a request, not a license condition).

New items on the pill (each off by default, #6157)

  • The Recycle Bin: how many items; open it, or empty it with a second click; always shown, or only once what's in it weighs 100 MB, 500 MB, 1 GB or 5 GB.
  • A timer, a stopwatch (with hundredths) and Pomodoro, each on its own (all three can run at once), in a panel like the macOS Clock app: lengths in hours, minutes and seconds on wheels (the mouse wheel, a drag or typed), a ring while it runs, Pomodoro's focus and break chosen; the pill shows the one ending first, in orange, and a click on it lists every one going as Live Activities like the iPhone's (each with its time, Pause and Cancel, the next alarm with its switch, Show all); a notice when each ends, with Repeat and Stop (Pomodoro: Stop and OK); and alarms in the same panel: a time each day on wheels, each on or off, with or without a sound, edited with a pencil, its notice with Stop (its sound repeats until then, a minute at most); alarms ring and timers end on time also behind a full-screen app or while the island restarts, and each Windows account has its own; Control Center buttons for the stopwatch, Pomodoro and alarms (#6156).
  • The network's speed, up and down.
  • An audio visualizer: six rounded bars jumping with the beat of the playing app's own sound (or any sound, like VLC's) while something plays, or swaying smoothly like the iPhone's (an option), with a sensitivity slider and a color (the icons', Windows' accent, a rainbow, your own or the cover's).
  • World clocks: Windows' own additional clocks (Date & time settings), shown as soon as they're added there, with a day ahead or behind marked; a click opens Windows' list of them.
  • The time until the next event, alarm, timer or Pomodoro part (each can be left out; in the next 12 hours); a click opens it.
  • The pill filling like a loading bar (each an option, off by default, in the Animations tab): with the progress apps show on their taskbar button (downloads, copies, installs; #6071, read from the taskbar's own progress bar), and with a laptop's battery charge while it charges (not while it's held at a charge limit, like 80%); one bar across the Fixed style's notches (the whole bar in the Bar style), a solid line under it like the taskbar's; a color for each kind (downloads and other apps, Windows' file copies, the battery: green, blue, Windows' accent or your own; red for an error, yellow paused); it moves simply, as a liquid wave or as a glow with particles; paused it breathes, an error shakes, done flashes with a check, canceled drains back.
  • Song lyrics (an option, off by default, goes online: each song's title and artist are sent to lrclib.net): the line sung now on the pill, in time with the song (its size, color and longest line chosen; or in the song title's place while a line is sung, an option), and all of them in a panel where a line clicked goes there in the song. Only for songs (with an artist, 45 s to 20 min, not videos or voice messages), and "Apps that look for lyrics" lists the apps seen playing as cards with their icons, each one's lyrics turned off with its switch; a search result is taken only when its title, artist and length match.

Status notices (from the pill, an option, off by default)

  • The charger plugged in, the battery under 20% and 10%, a Bluetooth audio device connected, and "Do not disturb" turned on or off (#6158, #6204); on the main island, also when it doesn't show the apps' notifications.

Tray icons

  • The grid of the icons not pinned has its own number of columns (6 as before, #6162).

Languages

  • The island and Windhawk's settings in German, Spanish, Russian and Japanese too (#6472), chosen in the island's settings or like Windows' display language; the dates follow them.

Settings

  • The island's settings open in a window of their own, like Windows' Settings (the gear under the island and the control center's): a side bar with the search and a tab per subject (also Dock, About and Logs), each option on a card with a line saying what it does, the island's preview at the top (its items in their order, dragged to move them), resizable, in the island's colors over Mica. A dimmed option says why under its name, and a click there goes to what it needs. Logs copies or saves a summary, the settings and the island's last 300 log lines without turning on Windhawk's logs.
  • Clearer texts for the two options that hide the clock and the tray (the Windows taskbar's, with the island; the dock's, without it).
  • The Monitors page: where the island appears as three buttons that say what they do, the screens as a bigger map (the islands marked), and with an island on every monitor a card for each (its notifications, its look).
  • One settings window a monitor (a notch opens its monitor's), opened at its own monitor's size, and back where it was after the island starts again.
  • A What's new tab (between About and Logs) with the notes of every published version (2.0.0, 2.0.1, 2.0.6 and 2.1.0) for users, in the island's 7 languages, switched by flags the mod draws itself (Direct2D shapes, nothing downloaded); it opens in the island's language, and the search finds the notes. The language buttons in General show the flags too.
  • Once per version (also on a first install), 10 seconds after the main island starts, a notice from the pill says what's new and stays until one of its buttons opens that tab or closes it (an option, on by default, per profile). The language buttons' flags sit on whole pixels, sharp at 150% and 175% too.

Control center

  • Every pill item that opens something can also be a control center button (hidden until added with Edit): notifications, calendar, what's playing, power, CPU/RAM use, profiles, keyboard language, privacy, USB drives, virtual desktops, folders, wallpaper, komorebi's layout, world clocks, next event, Recycle Bin, timer and the tray icons.
  • The magnifier, the narrator and the new on-screen keyboard are buttons that start them (their state wasn't always read right; the magnifier falls back to Win+Plus when it doesn't start); the on-screen keyboard can also go on the control center and the pill (#6160).

Brightness

  • A laptop's own screen has its slider and wheel too (through WMI, like Windows' own slider), beside monitors with DDC/CI; a monitor without DDC/CI shows none, as before (#6436, #6457, #6501, #6350).
  • The wheel on the brightness adds up small turns (touchpads, smooth wheels) instead of losing them (#6420).

Fixes

  • The island's window no longer reaches 3 pixels into a monitor above its own (it kept that monitor's dock from coming up at the middle of its edge).
  • Panels stay inside their monitor and never as tall as it (a long list went past the screen's bottom, into the next monitor, and Wallpaper Engine took it for a full-screen app and stopped).
  • Win+N and Win+A open on the main island wherever the mouse is; minimizing a notification sets its app aside on every island.
  • Every item on the pill grows in and shrinks away (the tray, the media's parts, the uses, the app in focus, the folders, the minimize button and the percentages used to jump); a group whose contents change size follows them smoothly.
  • The Bar style scrolls through its items when they don't fit; the control center has no limit of eight and grows wider to fit the screen.
  • A notification's app icon missing right after a restart is looked for again within seconds.
  • Closing a virtual desktop from the desktops' list closes that one, also when it's a few desktops away, and goes back to where you were (#6164).
  • The network item no longer shows a cable on Wi-Fi when Windows doesn't give the Wi-Fi's details (#6361).
  • The Task Manager button opens it also with an administrator's window in front (it pressed Ctrl+Shift+Esc, which Windows dropped then).
  • The dock comes up only with the mouse at the screen's bottom edge again; the strip above the edge counts only with another monitor below (#6472).
  • A Windhawk setting chooses the height over the bottom edge that brings the dock (or the transparent taskbar) up (in pixels at 100% scale), the same on every monitor; 0, the default, keeps it automatic (#6472).
  • The minimized line's invisible strip is half as thick: the mouse passing near the edge no longer brings the island back (#6468).
  • The control center's Emoji and Clipboard buttons open for the app in front, instead of closing at once.
  • While a panel opened from the pill is open, the pill keeps its width (a longer or shorter media title scrolls in it) and resizes once the panel closes, so the panel's corners stay put; one wider than the pill closes up before narrowing, so its contents aren't cut at the sides.
  • Right after Windows starts, the progress fill waits 30 seconds (apps restoring themselves reported a progress they didn't have and filled the whole bar).
  • A taskbar button without an app ID for a moment no longer makes its badge blink or loses the taskbar's own picture.
  • The dock no longer shows the plate the taskbar stacks behind an app with more windows, and an overlay picture (like a browser profile's photo) stays sharp at its own size as the icon grows.
  • With the timer's item on the pill, the next event item no longer shows the timer and Pomodoro too.
  • The progress fill reaches into the notches' curves.
  • The progress fill follows only what the taskbar's buttons show, read again every second while it shows (it no longer stays after an app has finished), and a new progress fills the pill after 5 seconds (Windows' file copies at once).
  • The visualizer follows the playing app's loudest audio session (a browser has several), and the output's sound while that app is paused or quiet, instead of staying still.
  • Turning the mod off puts the taskbar's auto-hide back only once Windows confirms it (and tries again later if it didn't), each taskbar button keeps its own app's icon and badge, and one taskbar element failing no longer stops the rest of the cleanup.
